title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1986 manuscript 'Réseaux via découpages', part of Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) programme. L is a one-dimensional tame 'line', an interval-like space that is totally ordered and may have endpoints ∂L. Previous pages show that a tame subset X of L whose 'transversal positions' T_i are all open and closed is either empty or all of L. This page is a remark ('NB').

Statement: let (X_α) be a finite family of tame subsets of L that are mutually tame. 'Mutually tame' is defined by requiring that S = ∪_α Ẋ_α be a finite totally ordered set t_1 < ... < t_n. Here Ẋ_α is most plausibly the frontier, or the set of 'special points', of X_α; the machine reading X_α° (interior) cannot be right. Grothendieck then claims that the Boolean algebra generated by the X_α has as its 'components' (atoms) the following tame convex sets, listed in increasing order: [L<t_1], {t_1}, ]t_1,t_2[, {t_2}, ..., {t_n}, [L>t_n]. The first and last pieces occur only when t_1 ∉ ∂L, respectively t_n ∉ ∂L. Hence the algebra depends only on S, that is, on a finite 'découpage' (subdivision) of L by points.

In modern terms: a finite family of definable subsets of an o-minimal line determines a finite partition of the line into points and open intervals (1-dimensional cell decomposition), and each set is a union of cells. The remark prepares page 40. There the goal is to characterise an ordered interval as a 'réseau' through betweenness data: pairs {a,b} and the components of {x : {a,x},{b,x} ∈ S}. Grothendieck notes this must be classical (Hilbert's order/betweenness axioms).
errors: As literally stated, the claim is too strong. The Boolean algebra generated by the X_α alone need not have the listed intervals and points as atoms. Counterexample: L = [0,1], X = [0,1/3] ∪ [2/3,1]. Its frontier is S = {1/3, 2/3}, but the algebra generated by X has only the atoms X and ]1/3,2/3[. The claim holds if one either passes to connected components of the atoms (the word 'composantes' in quotes suggests this is meant) or speaks of the finest tame partition subordinate to S. Read this way, the correct statement is that every X_α is a union of the listed cells. The algebra generated by the X_α is a subalgebra of the one determined by S, not equal to it.
The reading of X_α° as interiors would make the hypothesis absurd (a finite set of points cannot be a union of interiors of nonempty open pieces); it must be frontiers or special points.

ideas.what: A finite family of tame subsets of a tame line is subordinate to a finite subdivision by points t_1<...<t_n; the cells are points and open intervals, plus end intervals when the t_i are not endpoints.
ideas.modern_name: o-minimal (1-dimensional) cell decomposition; finite unions of points and intervals
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (1984), Pillay–Steinhorn (1986), Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn; semialgebraic case classical (Łojasiewicz)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5; no such explicit lemma there to my knowledge

ideas.what: Encoding the tame structure of L via a 'découpage' (finite subdivision) S, so that the relevant Boolean algebra depends only on S.
ideas.modern_name: Boolean algebra of definable subsets of a line as a direct limit over finite subdivisions (interval algebra)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine remark on the 1-dimensional case of tame (o-minimal-type) topology. It is mildly interesting as documentation of Grothendieck developing tame topology 'via découpages' in 1986, but it is mathematically elementary and well covered by o-minimality.
transcription_corrections: 'X_\alpha^\circ' in S = ∪ X_α should probably be read as Ẋ_α (frontier / special points), not interior.
The marginal notes '| si t_1 ∉ ∂L' and 'si t_n ∉ ∂L' qualify the end pieces [L<t_1] and [L>t_n] respectively.
Final lines are approximately: 'i.e. de points t_1<...<t_n (ou "découpage de L", subdivision ... des transversales)'; the word 'latérale' is doubtful.
